renders.prompt: Explain the argument of this song as if to a bright 10-year-old. Use ONLY the claims in the ESSENCE list below; every paragraph must correspond to at least one essence item (record indices). Do not add doctrines, comparisons, meta-commentary, or quoted terms. ESSENCE: [0] Bhairava is established as all-pervading conscious reality: one, endless, beginningless — the Absolute that pervades moving and unmoving states. [1] The Lord is then venerated as refuge of the helpless by a mind become His — veneration as mental absorption, not ritual offering. [2] The nirukta of Bhairava (bearing/supporting, the Roar of AHAM, benefactor of the terrified) is here performed, not stated: the name is lived. [3] Total surrender is sized to its object — the all-pervading consciousness is venerated by absorption into it.

paragraphs.text: First the song establishes who Bhairava is: consciousness itself, spread through everything that moves and everything that stands still — one, without end, without beginning. That is the Absolute.

Then it bows to Him — but not with flowers or rituals. The worship here is becoming: your mind turns into His, and that is how a helpless person takes refuge. The old unpacking of His name — the Bearer, the great Roar of I, the friend of the frightened — is not explained, it is lived. And the surrender fits its object exactly: only absorption is big enough for the all-pervading.

paragraphs.text: All-pervading conscious reality first: one, endless, beginningless, moving and unmoving both pervaded. Absolute established.
Then veneration as absorption, not offering: mind become His, refuge of the helpless. Nirukta performed, not stated. Surrender sized to object.
